title: Academor SAT Practice Test 1 Reading and Writing

questions.question:
Although the Atacama Desert receives almost no rainfall, its coastal hills are not entirely barren: fog drifting in from the Pacific Ocean provides enough moisture to ______ small communities of lichens and cacti that could not otherwise survive there.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: sustain
obscure
relocate
imitate
questions.correct: sustain
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The fog supplies the moisture that keeps the lichens and cacti alive, so it sustains them.

questions.question:
Critics who expected choreographer Lin Bao's new work to repeat the elaborate spectacle of her earlier productions were surprised by its ______: the piece features a single dancer, a bare stage, and no music other than the sound of the performer's breathing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: extravagance
familiarity
austerity
ambiguity
questions.correct: austerity
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

One dancer, a bare stage and no music describe severe simplicity, or austerity, the opposite of the expected spectacle.

questions.question:
Historians long assumed that medieval European farmers rarely traveled beyond their own villages, but recent analyses of market records have ______ that view, showing that many farmers regularly journeyed dozens of kilometers to sell produce at regional fairs.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reinforced
complicated
anticipated
popularized
questions.correct: complicated
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Evidence of regular long journeys runs against the old assumption, so the records have complicated it.

questions.question:
The novelist had grown accustomed to ______ reviews: critics typically acknowledged her technical skill but rarely expressed real enthusiasm for her books. She was therefore surprised when her third novel, which she considered her least ambitious, was praised effusively.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: scathing
rapturous
anonymous
lukewarm
questions.correct: lukewarm
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Reviews that admit skill but lack enthusiasm are lukewarm; “scathing” is too harsh and “rapturous” contradicts the text.

questions.question:
Many people assume that bees locate flowers primarily by sight. Yet when researchers scented artificial flowers but painted them the same dull gray as the surrounding background, bumblebees still visited the scented flowers far more often than unscented ones. Such findings suggest that, for bumblebees at least, odor can be as important a cue as color.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a common assumption that the text goes on to defend.
It describes a method that the researchers later rejected as unreliable.
It summarizes a conclusion that the final sentence of the text calls into question.
It presents an observation that challenges the assumption described in the previous sentence.
questions.correct: It presents an observation that challenges the assumption described in the previous sentence.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The experiment shows bees finding flowers without visual cues, which challenges the assumption that they rely mainly on sight.

questions.question:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Teodora has just arrived at her grandmother's apartment for the first time in many years.

The hallway smelled exactly as Teodora remembered: of floor wax, of oranges, of something sweet baking just out of sight. She had expected the place to seem smaller, the way childhood places are supposed to, but instead it seemed to have grown, as if the years she had been away had been quietly added to its rooms. On the wall hung the same faded photograph of the harbor, crooked by the same few degrees.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe a character's impression that a familiar place is unchanged in some respects but seems different in others
To explain why a character has avoided visiting a relative for many years
To contrast a character's memories of a place with her grandmother's memories of it
To show that a character is disappointed by the condition of an apartment she once admired
questions.correct: To describe a character's impression that a familiar place is unchanged in some respects but seems different in others
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The smells and the crooked photograph are unchanged, while the apartment unexpectedly seems larger.

questions.question:
Text 1

For decades, many linguists held that infants learn the sounds of their native language mainly by hearing speech directed at them. On this view, the slow, exaggerated “baby talk” that caregivers use is the primary source of the input infants need.

Text 2

Psycholinguist Amara Okafor and colleagues recorded the full daily sound environments of 40 infants and found that speech directed at the infants made up less than a fifth of the language they heard. Yet infants in households with more overheard conversation —speech between adults—developed sound discrimination abilities faster than other infants did, even when the amount of speech directed at them was similar.

Based on the texts, how would Okafor and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that infants need slow, exaggerated speech in order to learn any language sounds at all
By arguing that the view overlooks the contribution that speech not directed at infants may make to their learning
By suggesting that the view is correct for most infants but not for those who hear little adult conversation
By claiming that caregivers rarely use slow, exaggerated speech when talking to infants
questions.correct: By arguing that the view overlooks the contribution that speech not directed at infants may make to their learning
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Text 2 finds that overheard adult conversation speeds learning, which the infant-directed view in Text 1 ignores.

questions.question:
Foresters have traditionally treated dead trees in managed forests as a fire hazard to be cleared away. But a growing body of research shows that standing dead trees, or snags, provide nesting cavities for woodpeckers and owls, while fallen logs retain moisture during droughts and gradually return nutrients to the soil as they decay. As a result, some forest agencies now require that a minimum number of snags and logs be left in place after a harvest.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Dead trees pose a greater fire risk in managed forests than foresters once believed.
Woodpeckers and owls depend more heavily on dead trees than other forest animals do.
Research on the ecological benefits of dead trees has led some forest managers to change their practices.
Fallen logs are more beneficial to forests than standing dead trees are.
questions.correct: Research on the ecological benefits of dead trees has led some forest managers to change their practices.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text moves from the old view, to research on the benefits of dead trees, to the resulting change in policy.

questions.question:
The following text is adapted from a short story.

Mr. Halloran ran the town's only bookshop as if it were a lending library he resented. He would sell you a book, certainly, but only after asking what you intended to do with it, and if your answer displeased him, he might steer you toward something “more suitable” from a shelf near the back. Regular customers learned to name a book they did not want and then accept whatever he recommended instead—which, more often than not, turned out to be exactly what they had been looking for.

According to the text, what is true about Mr. Halloran's regular customers?
options: They avoid the bookshop whenever possible because they dislike Mr. Halloran's questions.
They prefer borrowing books from a library to buying them from Mr. Halloran.
They frequently ask Mr. Halloran to order books that are not available in his shop.
They have developed a strategy for dealing with Mr. Halloran that usually leads them to books they want.
questions.correct: They have developed a strategy for dealing with Mr. Halloran that usually leads them to books they want.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

They name a book they do not want, accept his recommendation, and usually get what they were looking for.

questions.question:
Marine biologist Henrik Vaal hypothesizes that juvenile reef fish use the sounds produced by healthy coral reefs—such as the clicks of snapping shrimp and the grunts of adult fish—to locate suitable places to settle.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Vaal's hypothesis?
options: Juvenile reef fish settled near underwater speakers playing recordings of healthy reefs more often than near speakers playing no sound.
Snapping shrimp produce louder clicks at night than they do during the day.
Adult reef fish produce grunts primarily when defending their territories from rivals.
Healthy coral reefs contain a greater variety of fish species than degraded reefs do.
questions.correct: Juvenile reef fish settled near underwater speakers playing recordings of healthy reefs more often than near speakers playing no sound.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only choice A links reef sounds directly to where juvenile fish choose to settle.

questions.question:
Agricultural scientist Priya Raman and colleagues studied how features at the edges of fields affect pollinators visiting sunflower crops. They counted visits by bees and other pollinators to sunflowers in fields with no special margins, fields bordered by strips of wildflowers, fields bordered by hedgerows, and fields with both features. Raman's team concluded that combining the features was more effective than using either one alone: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: fields with flower strips averaged 9.8 visits per hour, compared with 4.2 visits per hour in fields with no special margins.
fields with both features averaged 13.5 visits per hour, more than fields with only flower strips (9.8) or only hedgerows (7.1).
fields with hedgerows averaged 7.1 visits per hour, fewer than fields with flower strips.
fields with no special margins averaged the fewest visits per hour, at 4.2.
questions.correct: fields with both features averaged 13.5 visits per hour, more than fields with only flower strips (9.8) or only hedgerows (7.1).
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The claim compares the combination with each single feature; only B makes that comparison.

questions.question:
A student studying native plants for a prairie-restoration project grew seeds of three species at three soil temperatures and recorded the percentage of seeds that germinated. The student concluded that purple coneflower and blue grama are better suited to warm soil than common yarrow is, since ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: at 20°C, common yarrow had a higher germination rate (78%) than either purple coneflower or blue grama did.
blue grama had the lowest germination rate of the three species at 10°C (3%).
at 30°C, both purple coneflower (81%) and blue grama (88%) had higher germination rates than common yarrow did (64%).
purple coneflower's germination rate increased from 8% at 10°C to 55% at 20°C.
questions.correct: at 30°C, both purple coneflower (81%) and blue grama (88%) had higher germination rates than common yarrow did (64%).
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

“Warm soil” points to the 30°C column, where both species beat yarrow.

questions.question:
In 2014, authorities began restricting nighttime lighting and foot traffic on Beach A, a nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles, while nearby Beach B remained unregulated. A researcher claims that the restrictions contributed to an increase in nesting on Beach A.

Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researcher's claim?
options: In 2010, the number of nests on Beach B was higher than the number on Beach A.
The number of nests on both beaches decreased between 2010 and 2014.
The number of nests on Beach A in 2022 was more than twice the number on Beach B in 2010.
After 2014, the number of nests on Beach A increased substantially, while the number on Beach B continued to decline slightly.
questions.correct: After 2014, the number of nests on Beach A increased substantially, while the number on Beach B continued to decline slightly.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Nesting rose on the regulated beach after 2014 but not on the comparison beach, which supports a link to the restrictions.

questions.question:
In laboratory experiments, the freshwater crustacean Daphnia grows protective spines and helmet-like head extensions when it detects chemicals released by predatory fish. Producing these structures requires energy that would otherwise go toward reproduction, and Daphnia raised in water without predator chemicals do not develop them. This suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the ability to develop protective structures only when predators are present allows Daphnia to avoid the costs of defense when it is unnecessary.
Daphnia that develop protective structures reproduce more quickly than those that do not.
predatory fish are unable to detect Daphnia that lack spines and head extensions.
Daphnia raised in water containing predator chemicals eventually lose the ability to reproduce.
questions.correct: the ability to develop protective structures only when predators are present allows Daphnia to avoid the costs of defense when it is unnecessary.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Defenses are costly and appear only when predators are detected, so the switch saves energy when no threat is present.

questions.question:
The collection of letters exchanged between the two astronomers, which were donated to the university archive in 2019, ______ new insight into how nineteenth-century scientists shared observations across great distances.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: offer
have offered
offers
are offering
questions.correct: offers
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The subject is the singular noun “collection,” so the verb is “offers.”

questions.question:
The Andean condor is one of the heaviest flying birds in the ______ it rarely flaps its wings, relying instead on rising columns of warm air to stay aloft for hours.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: world,
world;
world
world, which
questions.correct: world;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is needed.

questions.question:
Architect ______ designed the community center to stay cool without air conditioning by using thick earthen walls and a roof that channels breezes through the building.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Leila Haddad
Leila, Haddad
Leila Haddad,
, Leila Haddad,
questions.correct: Leila Haddad
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A title directly before a name is not separated from it by commas, and no comma belongs between the subject and its verb.

questions.question:
When the first transcontinental telegraph line in the United States was completed in 1861, it ______ the time needed to send a message from one coast to the other from about ten days to a matter of minutes.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: reduces
will reduce
has been reducing
reduced
questions.correct: reduced
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The event is completed and placed in 1861, so the simple past “reduced” is needed.

questions.question:
Sociologists studying neighborhood gardens have found that the gardens do more than supply fresh produce: by giving residents a shared project, ______ also strengthen social ties among people who might otherwise never interact.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it
they
this
one
questions.correct: they
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The pronoun refers to the plural “gardens,” so “they” is correct.

questions.question:
The museum's new exhibit focuses on three overlooked figures in the history of ______ a weaver who designed punched-card patterns, a mathematician who wrote early programs, and an engineer who built one of the first electronic memory systems.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: computing:
computing,
computing;
computing so
questions.correct: computing:
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A colon introduces the list that explains “three overlooked figures.”

questions.question:
Having spent nearly a decade observing chimpanzees in the wild, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the primatologist's book describes tool use in remarkable detail.
tool use is described in remarkable detail in the primatologist's book.
the primatologist describes tool use in remarkable detail in a new book.
remarkable detail about tool use is provided in the primatologist's book.
questions.correct: the primatologist describes tool use in remarkable detail in a new book.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The person who spent a decade observing must come right after the modifying phrase.

questions.question:
Many comets follow vast, elongated orbits that take thousands of years to complete. ______ short-period comets complete an orbit in less than 200 years; Comet Encke, for instance, returns to the inner solar system about every 3.3 years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
By contrast,
Therefore,
For example,
questions.correct: By contrast,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Short orbits are the opposite of thousand-year orbits, so a contrast is needed.

questions.question:
The Roman architect Vitruvius argued that buildings should possess three qualities: strength, usefulness, and beauty. Centuries later, his writings were rediscovered and eagerly studied by Renaissance architects. ______ his treatise became one of the most influential texts in the history of Western architecture.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Nevertheless,
As a result,
Meanwhile,
questions.correct: As a result,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The treatise's influence follows from its rediscovery and study, a cause-and-effect relationship.

questions.question:
Some bioluminescent fungi glow continuously, a puzzling trait because producing light consumes energy. One hypothesis holds that the glow attracts insects that then spread the fungi's spores. ______ in one experiment, artificial mushrooms fitted with green lights attracted significantly more insects than unlit ones did.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In support of this idea,
Despite this,
In other words,
Even so,
questions.correct: In support of this idea,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The experiment provides evidence for the hypothesis just stated.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Great Green Wall is an initiative launched by the African Union in 2007.
  • Its goal is to restore degraded land across the Sahel region of Africa.
  • The initiative originally aimed to plant a continuous line of trees across the continent.
  • Over time, its focus shifted to a mosaic of land-management practices, such as restoring grasslands and supporting farmers' water-harvesting techniques.

The student wants to explain how the Great Green Wall's approach has changed.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Great Green Wall, launched in 2007, aims to restore degraded land in Africa's Sahel region.
Initially focused on planting a continuous line of trees, the Great Green Wall now emphasizes a mosaic of land-management practices.
Water-harvesting techniques are one of the land-management practices supported by the Great Green Wall.
The African Union launched the Great Green Wall initiative in 2007.
questions.correct: Initially focused on planting a continuous line of trees, the Great Green Wall now emphasizes a mosaic of land-management practices.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only B describes both the original approach and the current one.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Mae Jemison earned a medical degree from Cornell University.
  • She served as a Peace Corps medical officer in Sierra Leone and Liberia.
  • In 1987, she was selected for NASA's astronaut program.
  • In 1992, she flew aboard the space shuttle Endeavour, becoming the first African American woman to travel to space.

The student wants to emphasize the historic significance of Jemison's 1992 mission.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mae Jemison, who earned a medical degree from Cornell University, was selected for NASA's astronaut program in 1987.
Before joining NASA, Mae Jemison served as a Peace Corps medical officer in Sierra Leone and Liberia.
When Mae Jemison flew aboard the space shuttle Endeavour in 1992, she became the first African American woman to travel to space.
Mae Jemison flew aboard the space shuttle Endeavour.
questions.correct: When Mae Jemison flew aboard the space shuttle Endeavour in 1992, she became the first African American woman to travel to space.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only C states what made the 1992 flight historic.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Reflecting telescopes use mirrors to gather and focus light.
  • Refracting telescopes use lenses.
  • A large lens can be supported only at its edges, so it can sag under its own weight and distort images.
  • A mirror can be supported across its entire back surface.
  • The largest refracting telescope built for regular research, at Yerkes Observatory, has a lens 102 centimeters (40 inches) in diameter.

The student wants to explain why the largest telescopes are reflecting telescopes.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Reflecting telescopes use mirrors, whereas refracting telescopes use lenses.
The refracting telescope at Yerkes Observatory has a lens 102 centimeters in diameter.
Large lenses can sag under their own weight because they can be supported only at their edges.
Because a mirror can be supported across its entire back surface while a large lens sags when held only at its edges, the largest telescopes use mirrors rather than lenses.
questions.correct: Because a mirror can be supported across its entire back surface while a large lens sags when held only at its edges, the largest telescopes use mirrors rather than lenses.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Only D gives the reason (support and sagging) and connects it to the conclusion.

questions.question:
Though the poet's later work is often described as radically experimental, a careful reading reveals that it is ______ the formal traditions she claimed to reject: her fragmented lines frequently conceal the meter and rhyme schemes of classical sonnets.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: incompatible with
suffused with
unconcerned with
contemporaneous with
questions.correct: suffused with
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Hidden sonnet meter and rhyme mean the work is thoroughly permeated by tradition, or suffused with it.

questions.question:
Economist Tomás Ibarra argues that the popular image of the lone inventor is ______: most major innovations, he contends, emerged from networks of collaborators whose contributions were later attributed to a single, celebrated individual.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: inevitable
ambitious
apt
misleading
questions.correct: misleading
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

If the credit really belongs to networks, the lone-inventor image gives a false impression.

questions.question:
The archaeological team's initial conclusions about the settlement were necessarily ______: having excavated only a small fraction of the site, the researchers acknowledged that further digging could substantially revise their account of how its inhabitants lived.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: provisional
unanimous
exhaustive
derivative
questions.correct: provisional
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Conclusions that further digging could revise are temporary, or provisional.

questions.question:
Although the treaty was hailed at the time as a decisive diplomatic achievement, historians have since noted that its provisions were so ______ that each signatory could interpret them as supporting its own, often contradictory, territorial claims.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: punitive
stringent
equivocal
belated
questions.correct: equivocal
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Language that supports contradictory readings is open to more than one interpretation: equivocal.

questions.question:
Bird migration has often been described as a feat of instinct, with each species following a fixed, inherited route. Studies of the Eurasian blackcap complicate this picture. Since the 1960s, a growing number of blackcaps breeding in central Europe have begun wintering in Britain rather than in Spain, a shift that became viable as backyard bird feeders grew common. Remarkably, the offspring of these birds inherit the new direction: when raised in captivity, they orient toward Britain even without ever having made the journey.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides evidence that a recently developed migratory behavior has become heritable.
It explains why blackcaps were originally unable to survive winters in Britain.
It suggests that captive-raised birds are unreliable subjects for migration research.
It challenges the claim that blackcaps have changed their wintering grounds.
questions.correct: It provides evidence that a recently developed migratory behavior has become heritable.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Captive-raised young that orient toward Britain show the new route is passed on genetically.

questions.question:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Ines, a violinist, is preparing for an audition.

For weeks Ines had practiced the concerto's opening until she could play it in her sleep, and some nights, she suspected, she did. Her teacher praised the precision of her fingering, the evenness of her bow. Then, at their last lesson, he asked her to play it once more, “but this time as if you had never heard it before.” Ines lifted the violin and found, to her dismay, that she did not know how.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a teacher's criticism of a student and then shows the student rejecting that criticism.
It recounts a character's early failures and then describes how she eventually overcame them.
It contrasts a character's confidence before an audition with her nervousness during it.
It describes a character's thorough preparation and then reveals a limitation that this preparation has created.
questions.correct: It describes a character's thorough preparation and then reveals a limitation that this preparation has created.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Endless repetition has made the piece so familiar that Ines can no longer play it as if it were new.

questions.question:
Text 1

Many economists argue that minimum wage increases inevitably reduce employment, since employers faced with higher labor costs will hire fewer workers. Studies that find no job losses after modest increases, these economists contend, simply fail to capture effects that emerge over longer periods.

Text 2

Labor economist Ruth Adeyemi notes that in markets where a few large employers dominate hiring, those employers can hold wages below the value of what workers produce. In such markets, Adeyemi argues, a moderate minimum wage increase can actually raise employment by drawing more people into jobs that now pay enough to make working worthwhile.

Based on the texts, how would Adeyemi (Text 2) most likely respond to the economists' argument in Text 1?
options: She would agree that minimum wage increases reduce employment but argue that the reductions are smaller than the economists claim.
She would contend that their reasoning assumes market conditions that do not hold in every labor market.
She would argue that the studies they criticize examined periods too long to detect employment effects.
She would claim that large employers typically pay wages above the value of what workers produce.
questions.correct: She would contend that their reasoning assumes market conditions that do not hold in every labor market.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Adeyemi identifies markets dominated by a few employers, where the “inevitable” job losses in Text 1 need not occur.

questions.question:
Chemist Saeko Mori and colleagues have developed a coating that allows glass to repair small scratches on its own. The coating contains microscopic capsules filled with a liquid polymer; when a scratch ruptures the capsules, the polymer flows into the gap and hardens on exposure to air. Although the coating restored the transparency of scratched samples in laboratory tests, the team notes that each region of the coating can heal only once, since the capsules there are emptied in the process, and that the coating has not yet been tested under the temperature swings that windows and screens routinely experience.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Mori's team has developed a self-healing coating for glass that shows promise, though it has limitations that may affect its practical use.
Self-healing coatings for glass are unlikely to be used commercially because they cannot withstand changes in temperature.
Liquid polymers are more effective than other materials at restoring the transparency of scratched glass.
Mori's team has determined that the coating can repair the same scratch repeatedly as long as it is exposed to air.
questions.correct: Mori's team has developed a self-healing coating for glass that shows promise, though it has limitations that may affect its practical use.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The text presents a successful test and two acknowledged limitations; B overstates an untested concern and D contradicts the text.

questions.question:
The following text is adapted from a novel. Arthur has worked as a clockmaker for decades.

Arthur no longer looked at the clocks when he repaired them; he listened. A healthy movement had a rhythm as distinctive as a voice, and he could tell from the faintest hesitation in its beat that a pivot had worn or a spring had weakened. Customers sometimes found this unsettling, watching him sit with his eyes half closed and a pocket watch held to his ear, as though the thing were confiding in him.

Based on the text, what is true about Arthur?
options: He can no longer see well enough to repair clocks by sight.
He prefers repairing pocket watches to repairing other kinds of clocks.
His long experience has given him the ability to diagnose problems in clocks by sound.
His customers distrust his skills and often take their clocks elsewhere.
questions.correct: His long experience has given him the ability to diagnose problems in clocks by sound.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

He identifies worn pivots and weak springs from the rhythm of the beat.

questions.question:
Some languages require speakers to mark grammatically how they know what they are reporting —for example, whether they witnessed an event themselves or heard about it from someone else. Linguist Esra Demir hypothesizes that speakers of such languages pay closer attention to the sources of their information than speakers of languages without this requirement do.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Demir's hypothesis?
options: Speakers of languages with required source marking recalled whether they had seen or been told about events more accurately than other speakers did, though both groups recalled the events themselves equally well.
Speakers of languages with required source marking produced longer descriptions of events than speakers of other languages did.
Children learning languages with required source marking begin using the markers later than they begin using other grammatical forms.
Some languages without required source marking have optional words, such as “apparently,” that indicate where information came from.
questions.correct: Speakers of languages with required source marking recalled whether they had seen or been told about events more accurately than other speakers did, though both groups recalled the events themselves equally well.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A isolates memory for information sources (not memory in general) as the difference between groups.

questions.question:
Plant breeder Amina Diallo tested three wheat varieties in fields that received normal rainfall and in fields subjected to drought. Diallo argues that farmers in regions where droughts are becoming more frequent should consider planting Sable, even though it is not the highest-yielding variety under normal conditions, because ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: Kestrel produced the highest yield of the three varieties under normal rainfall, at 6.8 tonnes per hectare.
Sable produced the lowest yield of the three varieties under normal rainfall.
Marlow's yield under drought was 4.2 tonnes per hectare, higher than Kestrel's.
under drought, Sable's yield fell only to 4.9 tonnes per hectare, the highest of the three varieties in those conditions.
questions.correct: under drought, Sable's yield fell only to 4.9 tonnes per hectare, the highest of the three varieties in those conditions.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The argument concerns drought performance; D shows Sable has the smallest drop and the highest drought yield.

questions.question:
Researchers have proposed that birds in cities sing at higher pitches so that their songs are not masked by low-frequency traffic noise. A team led by ornithologist Jonas Pettersson tracked the average minimum frequency of great tit songs at urban and forest sites over three decades, during which traffic at the urban sites increased steadily. The team claims that its data are consistent with the proposal.

Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the team's claim?
options: In 1990, the average minimum song frequency was nearly the same at urban and forest sites.
From 1990 to 2020, the average minimum song frequency rose steadily at urban sites, while at forest sites it stayed close to 3.9 kilohertz.
The average minimum song frequency at forest sites was lower in 1995 than in 1990.
The average minimum song frequency at urban sites in 2020 was higher than the frequency at forest sites in 1990.
questions.correct: From 1990 to 2020, the average minimum song frequency rose steadily at urban sites, while at forest sites it stayed close to 3.9 kilohertz.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Pitch rose only where traffic grew, while the quieter forest sites stayed flat.

questions.question:
Psychologist Nadia Kovac hypothesized that background sounds containing understandable words interfere more with reading than with arithmetic, because reading and processing speech draw on the same verbal resources. She measured participants' performance on reading and arithmetic tasks under four background conditions. The data support her hypothesis, since ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: arithmetic scores were higher with instrumental music (81%) than in silence (79%).
arithmetic scores were lower with background conversation (72%) than in any other condition.
compared with silence, reading scores fell by 14 or more percentage points in the two conditions that included words, whereas arithmetic scores fell by no more than 7 points.
in silence, reading scores (82%) were higher than arithmetic scores (79%).
questions.correct: compared with silence, reading scores fell by 14 or more percentage points in the two conditions that included words, whereas arithmetic scores fell by no more than 7 points.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The hypothesis compares the effect of words on reading with their effect on arithmetic; only C makes that comparison.

questions.question:
Fig trees and the wasps that pollinate them are known for an exclusive relationship: each fig species is typically pollinated by a single wasp species, and each wasp species can reproduce only inside the figs of its partner tree. However, genetic studies have revealed that in some regions two or more wasp species share a single fig species, and that some wasps occasionally pollinate figs of a species other than their usual partner. Because hybrid fig trees can result from such cross-pollination, these findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: fig trees would be unable to reproduce without the help of more than one wasp species.
wasps that pollinate multiple fig species produce more offspring than wasps that pollinate a single species.
hybrid fig trees are unable to attract any wasp pollinators.
the strict pairing of single fig and wasp species may be less universal than previously thought and could contribute to the emergence of new fig lineages.
questions.correct: the strict pairing of single fig and wasp species may be less universal than previously thought and could contribute to the emergence of new fig lineages.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Shared and cross-species pollination contradict a strict one-to-one rule, and hybrids could give rise to new lineages.

questions.question:
In the late 1870s, ______ observations of Mars led some astronomers to believe that the planet's surface was crisscrossed by artificial canals.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: astronomer Giovanni Schiaparellis'
astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli's
astronomer, Giovanni Schiaparelli's,
astronomer Giovanni Schiaparellis
questions.correct: astronomer Giovanni Schiaparelli's
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The singular possessive of “Schiaparelli” is “Schiaparelli's,” with no commas after the title.

questions.question:
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault—a facility built deep inside a mountain on a remote Norwegian ______ holds more than one million seed samples from around the world.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: island,
island;
island—
island
questions.correct: island—
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The supplementary phrase opened with a dash must be closed with a dash.

questions.question:
Among the most surprising discoveries at the cave ______ a set of bone flutes that researchers estimate to be more than 35,000 years old.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: was
were
have been
are
questions.correct: was
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

In this inverted sentence the subject is the singular “a set,” so the verb is “was.”

questions.question:
The novelist drafted each of her books by hand, often filling dozens of ______ only after completing a full draft did she type the manuscript and begin revising.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: notebooks,
notebooks
notebooks;
notebooks and
questions.correct: notebooks;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Two independent clauses need a semicolon; a comma alone creates a comma splice.

questions.question:
In 1928, while sorting through culture plates in his London laboratory, Alexander Fleming ______ that a mold growing on one plate had killed the bacteria surrounding it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: noticing
to notice
having noticed
noticed
questions.correct: noticed
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The sentence needs a main verb in the past tense: “noticed.”

questions.question:
Early photographers needed their subjects to remain still for several minutes during exposures. By the 1850s, ______ improved chemical processes had reduced exposure times to a few seconds.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: however
however,
however;
however:
questions.correct: however,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

“However” interrupts the clause here, so it is set off by commas on both sides.

questions.question:
The wingspan of the wandering albatross can exceed three meters, which is greater than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: that of any other living bird.
any other living bird.
any other living bird's wingspans.
those of any other living bird.
questions.correct: that of any other living bird.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A wingspan must be compared with a wingspan; the singular “that of” does this.

questions.question:
For much of the twentieth century, scientists assumed that the adult human brain could not generate new neurons. ______ studies beginning in the 1990s found evidence that new neurons form in the hippocampus, a region involved in memory.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
Similarly,
However,
For instance,
questions.correct: However,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The new findings contradict the earlier assumption.

questions.question:
Researchers have long hoped to produce spider silk, which is remarkably strong and elastic, on an industrial scale. Farming spiders the way silkworms are farmed has proven impractical, however: many species are territorial and will attack one another when housed together. ______ researchers have turned to genetically modified organisms, such as bacteria and silkworms, that can produce spider silk proteins.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Instead,
Likewise,
Nonetheless,
In comparison,
questions.correct: Instead,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Modified organisms replace the impractical option of farming spiders.

questions.question:
The Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977, was designed primarily to study Jupiter and Saturn during a mission expected to last about five years. ______ it far outlived that mission: in 2012, it became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Therefore,
However,
For example,
Similarly,
questions.correct: However,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Outliving a five-year plan by decades runs against what was expected.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Rosetta Stone was discovered in 1799 near the town of Rashid (Rosetta), Egypt.
  • It contains the same decree written in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
  • Scholars at the time could already read ancient Greek.
  • By comparing the Greek text with the hieroglyphs, Jean-François Champollion announced a breakthrough in deciphering hieroglyphs in 1822.

The student wants to explain why the Rosetta Stone was useful for deciphering hieroglyphs.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Discovered in 1799, the Rosetta Stone contains a decree written in three scripts.
Because the Rosetta Stone presents the same decree in hieroglyphs and in ancient Greek, which scholars could already read, it allowed them to use the Greek text to decipher the hieroglyphs.
Jean-François Champollion announced a breakthrough in deciphering hieroglyphs in 1822.
The Rosetta Stone was found near Rashid, Egypt, and contains text in Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
questions.correct: Because the Rosetta Stone presents the same decree in hieroglyphs and in ancient Greek, which scholars could already read, it allowed them to use the Greek text to decipher the hieroglyphs.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only B explains the reason: a known script beside an unknown one with the same content.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Tardigrades are microscopic animals known for surviving extreme conditions.
  • When their surroundings dry out, tardigrades lose most of their body water and enter a dormant state called cryptobiosis.
  • In cryptobiosis, a tardigrade's metabolism drops to less than 0.01% of its normal rate.
  • Wood frogs survive the winter by allowing up to about two-thirds of their body water to freeze.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between how tardigrades and wood frogs survive harsh conditions.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tardigrades and wood frogs can both survive conditions that would kill many other animals.
Tardigrades are microscopic animals, and wood frogs survive the winter by allowing some of their body water to freeze.
Whereas tardigrades survive drying out by losing most of their body water, wood frogs survive winter by allowing much of their body water to freeze.
In cryptobiosis, a tardigrade's metabolism drops to less than 0.01% of its normal rate.
questions.correct: Whereas tardigrades survive drying out by losing most of their body water, wood frogs survive winter by allowing much of their body water to freeze.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only C uses a contrast (“whereas”) between the two survival strategies.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Retrieval practice means trying to recall material from memory rather than simply rereading it.
  • In one well-known study, students read a passage and then either reread it or took a recall test on it.
  • When tested five minutes later, the students who reread the passage remembered slightly more.
  • When tested one week later, the students who took the recall test remembered substantially more.

The student wants to present the study's findings to an audience unfamiliar with retrieval practice, emphasizing its long-term benefit.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Retrieval practice has been examined by researchers in a well-known study.
Students who reread a passage remembered slightly more when they were tested five minutes later.
In one study, students who reread a passage and students who took a recall test on it were tested at two different times.
Retrieval practice—trying to recall material rather than simply rereading it—may not help much in the short term, but in one study it helped students remember substantially more a week later.
questions.correct: Retrieval practice—trying to recall material rather than simply rereading it—may not help much in the short term, but in one study it helped students remember substantially more a week later.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Only D defines the term for a new audience and highlights the one-week result.
